Practices.Summary: HubSpot's testing practice is to use React Testing Library as its official UI testing framework, emphasizing user-focused tests over implementation details. In the testing migration, they collected runtime usage metrics accross team and then categorize packages into buckets. The team migrated simpler packages first to reduce risk and learn the process, and then postpone complex packages temporarily so they could contain technical debt. The company migrated more than 76,000 tests from Enzyme to React Testing Library and runs frontend tests in the browser rather than JSDOM.

evidence.quote: in August of 2022, we announced Testing Library as our official UI testing framework and began our migration.
Over the next two and a half years, we migrated more than 76,000 tests from Enzyme to React Testing Library with virtually no automation.
We instrumented Enzyme’s render methods to collect runtime usage metrics and started to build a picture of Enzyme usage across teams. We were then able to divide packages into buckets
Our frontend test setup is unique compared to much of the open source ecosystem in that we exclusively run our frontend tests in the browser.

Practices.Summary: Migration Story: The hubspot testing team adopts Testing Trophy strategy when embracing React Testing Library. The Testing Trophy is a testing strategy that prioritizes integration tests as the best balance between confidence, and maintenance cost, while still using static, unit, and end-to-end tests appropriately. At first, they documented guides for writing tests with common libraries and developed tools to minimize test fixture. By adopting this philosophy, teams felt empowered to take on the migration. Then while maintaining documentation and planning to migrate tests for quarters, they created separate tickets to track the work. But that was a lot of manual effort, so they built an internal system called Monarch as a centralized hub

evidence.quote: We created guides for how to write tests that used the most common libraries in our stack, and developed tooling to minimize the toil of creating test fixtures and mock network payloads.
To keep teams in the loop with our overall progress, we shared quarterly updates with engineers.
we also surfaced migration progress within our test reporter to give engineers real-time progress reports

For a given team, we took all Enzyme tests across all of their repositories, divided them into equal chunks across the remaining quarters we had allocated to this effort, and created separate tickets per quarter to track the work.
Having a small team dedicated to this effort allowed us to focus on tasks that reduced migration friction and to reinforce testing best practices.

Practices.Summary: HubSpot uses Sidekick AI code reviewer with Judge Agent quality gate to reduce time to first feedback by 90%, peaking at 99.76% reduction. The Judge Agent evaluates reviews for succinctness, accuracy, and actionability before posting to GitHub, maintaining high signal-to-noise ratio.

evidence.quote: Our AI code reviewer catches real issues, understands HubSpot-specific context, and maintains a high signal to noise ratio, often leaving no comments at all.
Sidekick has reduced the time it takes for engineers to get feedback on their code by 90%, peaking at a 99.76% reduction in September.
The Judge Agent acts as a quality gate between Sidekick's initial review and the comments that ultimately appear on a GitHub pull request.

After Sidekick drafts a review, the agent receives that output and evaluates it against three core criteria: Succinctness: Is the feedback clear and to the point? Accuracy: Is the suggestion technically correct within the context of the codebase and change? Actionability: If the feedback includes a code suggestion, can it be applied directly without additional modification?
Only review comments that pass the judge's evaluation are posted to GitHub, and everything else is filtered out.
AI pull request reviews are triggered automatically when pull requests are created, marked ready for review, or when Sidekick is manually requested as a reviewer

During the Feb 2026 incident, standard health checks failed to detect a permissions error because endpoints returned successful HTTP 200 responses with incorrect data. The incident was declared 16 minutes after full rollout due to customer support surges, and engineers resolved it via a full automated rollback within 37 minutes total.

evidence.quote: HubSpot offers two distinct MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers — one for connecting any MCP-compatible AI tool or agent to your CRM, and one for building on the HubSpot Developer Platform.

We favor starting small and learning quickly by shipping. Problems go from ideation to product in hours or days, not weeks, and we're pragmatic about documentation and design practices that support our speed.

What makes this work well with AI models is its predictable structure and clear examples. When implementing similar tools, we've found that providing comprehensive examples in your tool descriptions dramatically improves the model's ability to generate correct queries.
